dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: tanūdeśe śūnyataiva kṣaṇamātraṃ vibhāvayet | nirvikalpaṃ nirvikalpo nirvikalpasvarūpabhāk ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: If, even for a single moment, one contemplates some region of the body as nothing but void, free of thought-constructs, one becomes thought-free and takes on the nature of the thought-free.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh reads tanūdeśa as the body taken as the limited empirical self and describes three stages: contemplating it without thought-constructs, becoming habitually thought-free, and finally entering the state of Bhairava, whose nature is thought-free. Wallis and Bäumer read tanūdeśa as 'any part (or point) of the body'. This door follows the 'any part of the body' reading and notes Singh's.
dharana.technique_name: A Moment of Void in the Body
dharana.instruction: For a moment, sense one part of the body, such as a hand, as empty space.

checked_against: The Mystery Within (2019), Session Two list: 'Dharana 23' = verse 46 (agrees with Singh)
The Mystery Within (2019), parallel translations: 'Dharana 23 • verso 46' (agrees)

verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.wallis_yukti: verse 46: Space in any body part (Y20 ~ C1)

source_disagreements: tanūdeśa: Singh reads 'the body (as the limited self)'; Wallis and Bäumer read 'any part or point of the body'. This door follows Wallis and Bäumer and records Singh.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 46 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: one chosen region of the body, felt as void (for example a hand)
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is one small region of the body felt, just for a moment, as empty space.
geometry.svg_hint: a faint body outline with one hand drawn as an open, empty outline
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Brief opening
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: one small region stops feeling solid for a moment, and the mind follows it into openness. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Choose one region and let it be empty for a moment
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: One region of the body felt as void, just for a moment
attention.secondary: The thought-free quality of that moment

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: If, even for a single moment, one contemplates some region of the body as nothing but void, free of thought-constructs, one becomes thought-free and takes on the nature of the thought-free.
adiyogi.method_summary: Choose one region of the body, such as a hand. For a moment, sense it as nothing but open space, without thinking about it. Let the moment end naturally; repeat a few times.

honesty.disclosure: Door 023 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 23 (verse 46) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 023 is dharana 23, verse 46. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
New door researched on 2026-10-06 on branch research/vbt-houses-2-7; awaiting guardian review.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Keep it brief and light; if numbness or unease appears, move the hand and feel it normally. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
